column1: # Romanized Hinglish spelling-variant lexicon  [Linear 298-13, owner: Sarvesh]
# One group per line, tab-separated:  group_label <TAB> variant <TAB> variant <TAB> ...
# The label is the conventional Devanagari-derived romanisation; the remaining
# fields are surface forms that occur in the wild for the same underlying word.
# It drives spelling_variant_burden, the project's novel metric. Each group is one
# word that a tokenizer sees as several unrelated vocabulary entries. The mean
# number of tokens paid per surface form is the direct measurement of the cost our
# central hypothesis claims is being mistaken for a data-scarcity problem.
# It is also the intended input to Shibin's normalized chrF++ (298-23). The same
# lexicon must drive normalisation and burden measurement, otherwise the two
# numbers stop being about the same thing and their divergence -- which we report
# as evidence of orthographic instability -- is not interpretable.
# Curation rules, so this stays defensible in the report
# 1. High-frequency function words and discourse particles first. These dominate
#    token counts, so they dominate the burden, and they are also the forms whose
# 2. Variants are attested forms, not generated permutations. Padding the groups
#    with plausible-but-unseen strings would inflate the metric for free.
# 3. No proper nouns and no English words. Named-entity spelling is a separate
#    failure category in the taxonomy and mixing it in here would confound them.
# 4. Groups stay lowercase. Case folding is handled by the consumer, not the file,
#    because the tokenizer's treatment of case is itself part of what we measure.
# v1, 24 Sep 2026. Seeded by hand from HinGE references and standard Hinglish
# orthography; scheduled to be extended from the frozen train split once 298-11
# lands, and to be frequency-ranked from that corpus rather than from intuition.
# Any extension is a versioned change to this file, never an in-place edit, so
# that an already-reported burden number stays reproducible.
